![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119121/assets/5a3961346a4bcb0d94e46caf6d6ed1253dc56fb4761db07b11829e329bc2fa8d.png)

Consider the part of parabola and constant vector field $F$ shown above. Let $C$ be the path where the part of parabola is traversed from $A$ to $B.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$
- ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$
- ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ gives the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along $C:$

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statements I is false, while statement II is true. As the particle moves from $A$ to $B,$ the force $F$ works against the particle for $x>0,$ while $F$  works with the particle for $x<0.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119121/assets/af80eab6427f376084301c03715fd098cfe4a1c816dcd72d3e1129cfa35ff29d.png)

 

By symmetry, the contribution to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ for $x<0$ is canceled out by the contribution for $x>0.$ So,

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.
$$

- Statement III is false. If we reverse the orientation of $C,$ then the situation with regards to the work done by $F$ is similar to the previous case.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119121/assets/a26ca79400bf30aa891543d30a052a6e8ec071ccb48fcd8c418fe0a713dad212.png)

 

So, ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
